info.title: User Service API
info.description: Reusable user-service foundation for content-oriented web products. Public operations are namespaced under /v1; the no-name email registration transition is /v2/auth/register.

keys.description: Active and retained public verification keys.

methods.description: Safe locally usable login methods without provider identifiers.

activeWorkflows.description: Only persisted active workflows; never inferred or fabricated.

get.description: Lightweight liveness probe. It proves the Worker and router are running without touching D1 or any other dependency.

default.description: Unexpected failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

get.summary: Read the current User account details
get.description: Returns only the current User’s optional Account Details through the live service session.

default.description: Authentication failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

patch.summary: Partially update the current User account details
patch.description: Atomically updates only explicitly allowed Account Details for the current User.

204.description: The Account Details update was committed.

default.description: Validation or authentication failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

post.description: Streams a JPEG, PNG, or WebP body of at most 2 MiB, 8192 pixels per axis, and 40 megapixels to private object storage. The service validates its bounded container structure and stores only an opaque service-route reference in Identity.

204.description: The photo reference was saved for the current User.

default.description: Validation, authentication, storage or configuration failure.

delete.description: Clears the current User photo reference and queues private-object cleanup durably.

204.description: The current User photo reference was cleared.

default.description: Authentication or storage failure.

get.description: Streams the referenced private photo only when the live session owns the User and photo reference.

200.description: The private photo bytes, streamed with its validated media type.

default.description: Authentication, ownership, object availability or storage failure.

post.description: Creates an unverified email/password identity when the deployment policy allows registration, and schedules a verification message through the application mail boundary. The account cannot establish a session until verification succeeds while the policy requires verified email.

default.description: Registration failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

post.description: Authenticates an email/password identity. While the deployment policy requires verified email, unverified accounts receive a machine-readable verification-required failure instead of a session.

200.description: Authenticated. The session travels in the Set-Cookie header.

default.description: Authentication failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

post.description: Marks the email address verified from the token delivered by the verification action. Clients extract the `token` query parameter from the action URL and submit it here. Invalid or expired actions fail safely without revealing token material.

default.description: Verification failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

post.description: Schedules a fresh verification message for an unverified email address without creating duplicate identities. The response is identical whether or not the address is registered, so it cannot be used for account enumeration.

default.description: Request failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

post.description: Schedules a password-reset message for the account matching the email address without creating identities. The response is identical whether or not the address is registered, so it cannot be used for account enumeration.

default.description: Request failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

post.description: Checks whether a password-reset token is current without consuming or mutating it. Unknown, expired, and already consumed actions return `valid: false`. Responses never include token material and are never cached.

200.description: Whether the password-reset action is current.

default.description: Check failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

post.description: Sets a new password from the token delivered by the password-reset action. Reset actions are single use and expire. Successful resets revoke existing sessions. Invalid, expired, reused, or malformed actions fail safely without revealing token material.

default.description: Reset failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

get.description: Returns the stable application-owned current-User representation for the session carried by the request cookies. Anonymous or invalid sessions receive the standard unauthenticated Problem Details response.

default.description: Authentication failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

post.description: Invalidates the session carried by the request cookies. Subsequent authenticated-only requests with that session no longer resolve a User.

default.description: Sign-out failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

post.summary: Issue or refresh presentation-only Reader State
post.description: Issues or refreshes short-lived signed Reader State from the live HttpOnly cookie session. The request carries no user, claims, issuer or audience. Reader State holds the opaque subject, stable issuer, Reader-State-specific audience, integer issued/expiry bounds and an empty entitlements list. Expiry never exceeds the live session expiry and is at most 15 minutes. Reader State is for presentation only and never authenticates or authorizes an endpoint. All responses are private, no-store.

200.description: The signed Reader State and its integer Unix expiry.

default.description: Issuance failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

get.description: Returns the active and retained public asymmetric verification keys as an RFC 7517 JSON Web Key Set. Private key material is never published. Responses carry bounded public caching; verification keys remain available through every outstanding token lifetime plus the documented clock tolerance.

default.description: Publication failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

get.summary: Publish effective authentication capabilities and password policy
get.description: Returns deployment-owned authentication capabilities and password creation policy. No secrets or provider configuration are included; the response is never cached.

default.description: Configuration failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

get.description: Returns the exact administrative representation for the session carried by the request cookies when that session holds User listing/read access. Anonymous or invalid sessions receive the standard unauthenticated Problem Details response; valid non-administrative sessions receive the forbidden Problem Details response. The public `/v1/me` representation is unchanged by this operation.

default.description: Authorization failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

get.description: Returns the stable application-owned administrative User representation in ascending email order with bounded server pagination and optional case-insensitive literal email substring search. Anonymous or invalid sessions receive the standard unauthenticated Problem Details response; valid non-administrative sessions receive the forbidden Problem Details response. The `total` counts all matches before pagination.

default.description: Authorization failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

get.description: Returns the stable application-owned administrative User representation for one opaque identifier. Anonymous or invalid sessions receive the standard unauthenticated Problem Details response; valid non-administrative sessions receive the forbidden Problem Details response even when the identifier does not exist. Authorized missing Users receive the not-found Problem Details response.

default.description: Authorization failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

get.description: Returns only allowlisted successful lifecycle events in newest-first order. Existing history is not backfilled, routine login/logout is excluded, and cursors are opaque.

403.description: The actor lacks authority or is disabled.

put.summary: Force the canonical Reader email verified
put.description: Marks only the current canonical Reader email verified and invalidates pending verification actions. It never sends mail or revokes Reader sessions.

200.description: The current canonical email verification state.

403.description: The actor is not allowed to perform the command.

409.description: The command conflicts with current Reader state.

500.description: The command could not be audited or completed.

503.description: Message scheduling failed after the command was committed.

post.summary: Schedule a Reader password recovery message
post.description: Schedules normal password recovery only for a Reader with a usable credential method. The Administrator never receives or sets the password.

202.description: The recovery message was accepted for scheduling.

get.summary: Read one User’s Account Details for administrators
get.description: Returns only the selected User’s optional Account Details to an authorized Administrator. Anonymous or invalid sessions receive 401; non-administrators receive 403 before target existence is disclosed; authorized missing Users receive 404.

default.description: Authorization or lookup failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

patch.summary: Update one User’s Account Details for administrators
patch.description: Atomically updates only allowlisted Account Details for the selected User. Unknown or Identity-owned fields reject the entire request.

200.description: The selected User’s updated Account Details.

default.description: Validation, authorization or lookup failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

post.description: Creates the first administrative User through the auth engine after migrations, using explicit operator-supplied credentials. Succeeds only while no administrator exists; repeats and conflicting identities fail with stable machine codes instead of duplicating privileged accounts. The bootstrapped administrator remains subject to the deployment email verification policy before signing in. Creation schedules its first verification message; delivery failure does not undo the administrator. A concurrent active bootstrap may return a retryable 409 while its lease is still held.

201.description: The first administrator was created and verification was requested.

default.description: Bootstrap failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

post.description: Deprecated compatibility alias for POST /v1/admin/auth/bootstrap. The request, authorization, first-Administrator claim and storage all belong exclusively to the Administrator realm.

201.description: The first Administrator was created and verification was requested.

default.description: Bootstrap failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

post.summary: Register an email identity without a public name
post.description: Creates an unverified email/password identity from email and password only. The full email address is used as Better Auth’s required technical name; Account Details remain unset until explicitly provided through their own operations.

default.description: Registration failure as RFC 9457 Problem Details.
